points.title: 音乐启蒙时期
points.description: 艾灵顿出生于华盛顿的中产阶级非裔家庭，从小接受良好的教育。他最初学习钢琴是为了取悦母亲，但很快展现出非凡的天赋。在华盛顿的种族隔离环境下，他学会了如何在白人主导的音乐世界中生存并发展自己的风格。这一时期，他受到了拉格泰姆音乐的影响，并开始在当地的酒吧和咖啡馆演奏，为日后的音乐生涯奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Born into a middle-class African American family in Washington, D.C., Ellington received a good education. Initially learning piano to please his mother, he quickly displayed exceptional talent. Growing up in the segregated environment of Washington, he learned how to navigate and develop his style within the white-dominated music world. During this period, he was influenced by ragtime music and began playing in local bars and cafes, laying the foundation for his future musical career.

points.title: 职业起步
points.description: 艾灵顿移居纽约，开始在哈莱姆区的音乐厅和俱乐部演出。他组建了自己的乐队，最初名为'Duke's Serenaders'，后来更名为华盛顿人乐队(Washingtonians)。这一时期，他发展出了自己独特的钢琴风格，融合了爵士、蓝调和古典音乐的元素。1923年，乐队录制了第一张唱片，标志着他职业音乐生涯的正式开始。在纽约的经历让他接触到了更广泛的音乐风格和表演机会，极大地拓展了他的音乐视野。
points.descriptionEn: Ellington moved to New York and began performing in theaters and clubs in Harlem. He formed his own band, initially called 'Duke's Serenaders,' later renamed the Washingtonians. During this time, he developed his distinctive piano style, blending elements of jazz, blues, and classical music. In 1923, the band recorded their first record, marking the official start of his professional music career. His experiences in New York exposed him to a wider range of musical styles and performance opportunities, significantly expanding his musical horizons.

points.title: 崛起与成名
points.description: 这一时期是艾灵顿音乐生涯的关键转折点。1927年，他的乐队在棉花俱乐部(Cotton Club)获得驻场演出机会，这是当时最负盛名的夜总会之一。通过广播，他们的音乐传遍了全美，使艾灵顿成为全国知名的音乐家。他创作了许多经典作品，如《Mood Indigo》和《It Don't Mean a Thing (If It Ain't Got That Swing)》。艾灵顿不仅是一位钢琴家和乐队领导者，更是一位作曲家，他开始为乐队中的每位音乐家创作个性化的作品，充分发挥他们的独特才能。这一时期，他的乐队成为最具创新性和影响力的爵士乐队之一。
points.descriptionEn: This period marked a crucial turning point in Ellington's musical career. In 1927, his band secured a residency at the Cotton Club, one of the most famous nightclubs of the time. Through radio broadcasts, their music reached audiences across the country, making Ellington a nationally known musician. He composed many classic works such as 'Mood Indigo' and 'It Don't Mean a Thing (If It Ain't Got That Swing)'. Ellington was not just a pianist and bandleader but also a composer who began creating personalized pieces for each musician in his band, fully utilizing their unique talents. During this time, his band became one of the most innovative and influential jazz ensembles.

points.title: 艺术成熟期
points.description: 艾灵顿进入了他创作的黄金时期，创作了一系列被称为'艾灵顿颂歌'的长篇管弦乐作品，如《Black, Brown and Beige》和《Harlem》。这些作品超越了传统的流行音乐范畴，融合了爵士、古典和福音音乐元素，展现了非裔美国人的历史和文化经历。他开始与作曲家比利·斯特雷霍恩(Billy Strayhorn)建立长期合作关系，后者成为他最重要的创作伙伴。艾灵顿的乐队在这一时期也达到了巅峰，培养了多位杰出的爵士音乐家，如约翰尼·霍吉斯(Johnny Hodges)和保罗·冈萨雷斯(Paul Gonzalez)。
points.descriptionEn: Ellington entered his golden period of composition, creating a series of extended orchestral works known as 'Ellingtonia,' such as 'Black, Brown and Beige' and 'Harlem.' These works transcended traditional popular music, blending jazz, classical, and gospel elements to depict the history and cultural experiences of African Americans. He began a long-term collaboration with composer Billy Strayhorn, who became his most important creative partner. Ellington's band also reached its peak during this time, nurturing many outstanding jazz musicians like Johnny Hodges and Paul Gonzalez.

points.title: 国际影响力
points.description: 二战后，艾灵顿的乐队开始频繁的国际巡演，将爵士乐带到世界各地。1956年，他们在纽波特爵士音乐节上的演出成为传奇，现场专辑《Ellington at Newport》大获成功。艾灵顿开始与交响乐团合作，创作了更多大型管弦乐作品，如《Such Sweet Thunder》和《Far East Suite》。他成为美国文化的重要使者，通过音乐促进不同文化间的理解。这一时期，他获得了多项荣誉，包括总统自由勋章，并成为第一位在白宫为总统表演的非裔美国音乐家。
points.descriptionEn: After World War II, Ellington's band began frequent international tours, bringing jazz music to audiences worldwide. Their 1956 performance at the Newport Jazz Festival became legendary, and the live album 'Ellington at Newport' was a major success. Ellington began collaborating with symphony orchestras, composing more large-scale orchestral works like 'Such Sweet Thunder' and 'Far East Suite.' He became an important cultural ambassador for the United States, promoting understanding between different cultures through music. During this period, he received numerous honors, including the Presidential Medal of Freedom, and became the first African American musician to perform at the White House for a president.

points.title: 晚年成就
points.description: 艾灵顿晚年继续创作和演出，尽管健康状况有所下降。他创作了三部神圣音乐会(Sacred Concerts)，将爵士乐与宗教音乐融合，展现了他对精神层面的探索。1970年，他在肯尼迪中心举办了纪念自己70岁生日的音乐会，多位知名音乐家参与演出。1973年，他获得了普利策音乐奖特别奖，成为首位获得此项荣誉的非裔美国人。艾灵顿于1974年在纽约去世，但他的音乐遗产持续影响着后世，被公认为20世纪最重要的作曲家之一和爵士乐的象征人物。
points.descriptionEn: In his later years, Ellington continued to compose and perform despite declining health. He created three Sacred Concerts, blending jazz with religious music, showing his exploration of spiritual dimensions. In 1970, he held a concert at the Kennedy Center to celebrate his 70th birthday, with many renowned musicians participating. In 1973, he received a special Pulitzer Prize for Music, becoming the first African American to receive this honor. Ellington died in New York in 1974, but his musical legacy continues to influence later generations, widely regarded as one of the most important composers of the 20th century and an iconic figure in jazz music.

appraisal.zh: 杜克·艾灵顿被公认为20世纪最具影响力的音乐家之一，他把爵士乐从舞蹈伴奏提升为复杂的艺术表达，身兼钢琴家、乐队领导者与多产作曲家，作品逾两千首，并以音乐呈现非裔美国人的文化身份与历史经历，成为优雅、创新与文化融合的象征，其影响跨越种族、阶级与国界。也有研究者指出，他的音乐有时偏于商业化，后期作品被认为深度与情感共鸣不足，在种族问题上立场偏温和，乐队管理亦被指过于独断、限制了年轻乐手的空间。
appraisal.en: Duke Ellington is widely regarded as one of the most influential musicians of the 20th century, elevating jazz from dance accompaniment to complex artistic expression; pianist, bandleader and prolific composer of more than 2,000 works, he gave musical voice to African American cultural identity and history and became a symbol of elegance, innovation and cultural fusion whose influence crossed race, class and borders. Some researchers note that his music was at times commercial, that his later works are judged lacking in depth and emotional resonance, that his stance on racial issues was moderate, and that his band management was autocratic, limiting younger players.

supporter.zh: 杜克·艾灵顿被誉为美国音乐的国宝，他将爵士乐提升到了艺术的高度，使其从娱乐音乐转变为严肃的艺术形式。他打破了种族界限，成为第一位在白宫为总统表演的非裔美国音乐家，为后来的非裔艺术家铺平了道路。艾灵顿的乐队不仅是音乐团体，更是一个培养人才的摇篮，他善于发掘每位音乐家的独特才能，为他们创作个性化的作品。他的音乐融合了多种风格，展现了非裔美国人的文化精髓，成为美国文化的重要组成部分。
supporter.en: Duke Ellington is revered as a national treasure of American music, elevating jazz to the status of art and transforming it from entertainment music into a serious art form. He broke racial barriers, becoming the first African American musician to perform at the White House for a president, paving the way for future African American artists. Ellington's band was not just a musical ensemble but a talent incubator; he excelled at discovering each musician's unique abilities and creating personalized works for them. His music blended various styles, embodying the essence of African American culture and becoming an integral part of American culture.

critic.zh: 批评者认为艾灵顿的音乐过于商业化，为了迎合大众口味而牺牲了艺术创新。一些评论家指出，他的作品虽然技巧精湛，但缺乏深度和情感共鸣，特别是在他后期作品中。此外，有人批评他在种族问题上的立场过于温和，没有积极参与民权运动，与同时代的爵士音乐家如迈尔斯·戴维斯相比显得不够激进。还有人认为他的乐队管理方式过于独断，限制了年轻音乐家的创新空间，导致乐队风格逐渐固化。
critic.en: Critics argue that Ellington's music was overly commercial, sacrificing artistic innovation to cater to popular tastes. Some commentators note that while his works were technically brilliant, they lacked depth and emotional resonance, particularly in his later compositions. Additionally, some criticize his stance on racial issues as too moderate, pointing out that he did not actively participate in the civil rights movement, appearing less radical compared to contemporary jazz musicians like Miles Davis. Others also argue that his band management style was too autocratic, limiting the creative space for younger musicians and causing the band's style to become increasingly rigid.

objective.zh: 从历史和文化视角看，杜克·艾灵顿是20世纪最具影响力的音乐家之一，他重新定义了爵士乐的可能性，将其从简单的舞蹈伴奏提升为复杂的艺术表达。他不仅是杰出的钢琴家和乐队领导者，更是一位多产的作曲家，创作了超过2000首作品。艾灵顿通过音乐展现了非裔美国人的文化身份和历史经历，为美国音乐增添了独特的维度。在流行文化中，他已成为优雅、创新和文化融合的象征，其音乐跨越了种族、阶级和国界，持续影响着全球音乐发展。
objective.en: From a historical and cultural perspective, Duke Ellington stands as one of the most influential musicians of the 20th century, redefining the possibilities of jazz by elevating it from simple dance accompaniment to complex artistic expression. He was not only an exceptional pianist and bandleader but also a prolific composer, creating over 2,000 works. Through his music, Ellington portrayed the cultural identity and historical experiences of African Americans, adding a unique dimension to American music. In popular culture, he has become a symbol of elegance, innovation, and cultural fusion, and his music continues to influence global musical development across racial, class, and national boundaries.

self.zh: 音乐是我的事业，但它是我的生命。
self.en: Music is my business, but it's my life.
